summary: Patrick Murphy is killed at the Montana Consolidated mine in Butte on the afternoon of 28 April 1890, when a bundle of lagging poles being lowered in a cage works loose and jams the shaft, crushing the lower part of his abdomen. Four other men — William Gray, Peter Leyden, Charlie Colston, and John Combs — are injured to varying degrees. A coroner's inquest before jurors and Coroner Beals returns a verdict that the accident was wholly unavoidable and exonerates the company; Murphy, a widower, leaves seven children, the eldest a ten-year-old boy already employed as a tool carrier in the same mine.
